newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Escondida copper output 1.4 mln T by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Escondida copper output 1.4 mln T by 2001.

text.p: Chile's Minera Escondida Limitada copper mine expects to boost output to 1.4 million tonnes a year by 2001 and to be at least 1.0 million tonnes in 2010, the firm's technical manager said Thursday.
Escondida, already the world's largest copper mine, will invest $2 billion over the next five to six years in expansion projects, Escondida's David Borries told a copper conference in Santiago.

Borries said that if all goes well, Escondida will start construction next April of a 125,000-tonne a year oxide ore heap-leaching project with the first cathode expected to be cast in August 1998. This project will cost $460 million.

The mine's phase four expansion, which will keep the main pit's production at 800,000 tonnes a year of copper produced from sulfide ores, is in a feasibility stage and should come into production in the year 2000, Borries said.
Another project, Escondida North, is in the prefeasibility stage and will come into production no earlier than 2001.

Borries said that no decision has yet been made on whether Escondida North, which will exploit an extension of the nearby Zaldivar mine's ore body, will produce concentrates by flotation or cathodes by heap-leaching.
Borries said that production would be at least 1.0 million tonnes in 2010, although it could be increased by a project known as "phase five", which is timetabled for 2007 or 2008.
"Now they like very good projects, but there could be changes in the timetable," Borries said.
The mine finished its most recent expansion, phase three, mid-year and its annual production is now about 800,000 tonnes.
